updates.summary: React 19.3.0 is a significant minor release introducing major new features including ViewTransition animations, Fragment Refs, and a new browser() API, alongside a large number of bug fixes across core React, DOM, SSR, and Server Components. The breadth of changes is extensive and touches nearly every subsystem of React. While the new features are additive and opt-in, the behavioral changes to transitions (now rendered independently rather than entangled) and numerous internal fixes may affect existing application behavior.
breakingChanges: Transitions now render independently instead of being entangled into a single render — a slow transition no longer holds up unrelated ones, which could change the perceived rendering order in apps relying on transition batching behavior.
react-server-dom-webpack/*.unbundled has been moved to private react-server-dom-unbundled, which may break existing imports if your project uses those unbundled entry points.
Trusted Types API integration is now enabled, which may affect apps that manage HTML content in ways incompatible with Trusted Types policies.
DEV-only warning added when a component appears to have been unblocked by calling use() conditionally — could surface new warnings in development builds for existing code patterns.
ramifications: Apps using transitions (useTransition, startTransition) may see changed rendering behavior due to independent transition rendering — visual sequencing and loading state timing could differ.
Server-side rendering pipelines have numerous fixes and changes; teams using react-dom/server or React Server Components should thoroughly test SSR output and hydration behavior.
The new Fragment Refs feature changes how refs interact with Fragment elements — existing assumptions about ref attachment may need review.
Fast Refresh behavior has been fixed in several ways that may cause components wrapped in lazy() or memo() to remount more aggressively during development.
Form and event handling changes (onReset, submit events with submitter, defaultValue for number inputs) may alter form behavior in subtle ways.
Activity (formerly Offscreen) has several fixes that change how hidden trees handle errors, portals, and store subscriptions — apps using Activity should be regression tested.
Performance impact is generally positive due to numerous optimizations in RSC payload parsing, Flight serialization, and transition rendering.
The new browser() API and onBrowserBailout option change the SSR/client handoff model and require careful integration if adopted.

updates.summary: React 19.3 is a significant minor release introducing major new features including ViewTransition animations, Fragment Refs, a new browser() API, and Trusted Types integration. While labeled as a minor update, the scope of changes is substantial — covering hundreds of PRs across React core, DOM, SSR, and RSC layers — warranting careful review before adoption. The release also includes notable behavioral changes such as independent transition rendering and numerous bug fixes that may affect existing application behavior.
breakingChanges: Transitions now render independently instead of being entangled into a single render — a slow transition no longer holds up unrelated ones, which may change perceived rendering behavior in apps relying on transition ordering.
Trusted Types API integration is now enabled, which may affect apps that set innerHTML or use certain DOM manipulation patterns in environments with a Trusted Types policy.
Move of 'react-server-dom-webpack/*.unbundled' to private 'react-server-dom-unbundled' package may break direct imports of those entry points.
StrictMode now double-invokes effects after Fast Refresh and during hydration, which could surface latent bugs in effect cleanup logic.
ramifications: ViewTransition and Fragment Ref APIs are new and additive, but their introduction involves deep changes to the React reconciler and DOM handling that could have subtle side effects.
Independent transition rendering changes the scheduling model; apps with complex concurrent features or animations may observe different timing or ordering of updates.
Numerous SSR and RSC fixes (abort handling, hydration mismatches, stream backpressure, Suspense boundary behavior) may change server rendering output or behavior in edge cases.
Form-related fixes (onReset, form status reset, submitter handling) could affect form components and server actions behavior.
Fast Refresh now correctly remounts components in more cases, which could surface previously hidden bugs in effect cleanup or component initialization.
Activity (Offscreen) component received multiple fixes around portal hiding, error containment, and metadata hoisting — behavior may change for apps using this API.
Context propagation into Suspense fallbacks and through suspended boundaries was fixed — apps relying on previous (buggy) behavior may see different context values.
useDeferredValue getting-stuck bug was fixed, which could change timing characteristics of deferred updates.
defaultValue handling for number inputs was updated to match other input types, potentially affecting controlled/uncontrolled input behavior.

updates.summary: This minor update includes several bug fixes, new feature enhancements to existing rules, and a performance improvement via fast paths in critical areas. The changes are mostly additive or corrective in nature, with no breaking changes indicated. The risk is low, though teams should verify any rule behavior changes around `object-shorthand`, `no-unsafe-finally`, and `new-cap` do not cause unexpected lint failures in their codebase.
ramifications: The `new-cap` rule now only exempts built-ins that reference the global scope, which may cause new lint errors for code that previously relied on broader exemptions.
The `no-unsafe-finally` rule now reports unsafe labeled `continue` statements, potentially surfacing new lint warnings or errors in codebases that use labeled loops inside finally blocks.
The `object-shorthand` rule now handles quoted properties for `ignoreConstructors`, which may change linting behavior for code using quoted constructor property names.
Bug fixes to `prefer-object-spread` and `object-shorthand` for `__proto__` properties may suppress previously reported (possibly false positive) lint errors.
Performance improvements via fast paths may reduce linting time in large codebases.
Documentation clarification around `--cache` and stale results for cross-file rules may prompt teams to reconsider their CI caching strategies.

updates.summary: TypeScript 7.0 is a major version release representing a significant architectural shift, as it is based on the new Go-native rewrite (typescript-go), rather than the original TypeScript codebase. This introduces substantial performance improvements but also potentially significant breaking changes in type checking behavior, compiler APIs, and tooling compatibility. Upgrading requires thorough testing of your entire codebase, especially custom tooling, plugins, or programmatic uses of the TypeScript compiler API.
